newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt vols firm ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt vols firm ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: U.S. interest rate options volatilities firmed, supported by an approaching flurry of U.S. economic data, beginning with the first-quarter employment cost index on Tuesday.

The rate of implied volatility for June at-the-money straddles climbed to 9.38 percent at the close of Monday's session from 9.11 percent at Friday's settlement. September volatility was 9.40 percent, unchanged from the previous session.
Volatility rose despite the day's quiet activity in the underlying futures, with the June bond contract drifting higher late to end at 107-13, up 9/32.
"Everybody's just sitting on their hands waiting for all the numbers to come up," said one bond analyst at a U.S. brokerage firm.
The full calendar has raised the hopes of options analysts looking for more dramatic price movement to support volatility than has been seen in recent sessions.

Other reports punctuating the week include March durable goods on Tuesday, first-quarter advance gross domestic product on Wednesday, the national purchasing managers April survey and personal income and consumption data on Thursday, and April nonfarm payrolls on Friday.
Bond futures' tight ranges and sideways action of late have frustrated many market participants. However, analysts noted, such movement can often serve as the springboard for a major spike in prices.
"It has been a grind to endure, but it all adds pressure to the next move," said a second brokerage house analyst.

At the short end of the yield curve, volatilities for quarterly options on the most-active Eurodollar futures contracts late in the session were unchanged from Friday at 11.2 percent in September and 12.6 percent in December.

However, the rate of volatility on short-dated June mid-curve options jumped 1.6 point to 17.6 percent, erasing all of the previous session's sharp decline. September mid-curve volatility held steady at 16.6 percent.
